Subject: Quick follow up + volumes & marketplace asks

Hi Karthik —

Good chat earlier, thanks for walking through Redwood’s serving options. A few things I promised to capture so we’re aligned:

- High-level usage: production inference for our chat assistant (English + fr + es).
  - Baseline: ~250M tokens/month (steady state)
  - Peak/day: up to ~1.2B tokens (marketing events)
  - Expected growth: 20–30% q/q next 12 months
- Primary constraint: we need predictable unit economics (target $/1M tokens) for budgeting.
- Procurement ask: we prefer to buy via AWS private offers (Marketplace) but will consider GCP/Azure private pricing if mapping to a clear unit rate is possible.

Two asks for Redwood: can you map what a private-offer unit $/1M tokens would look like on AWS vs your hosted list price (and how Reserved/Dedicated commitments translate)? Also — can you send a simple template we can fill with month-by-month forecast?

We’d like to get a pricing workshop on the calendar next week if possible (Mike + CFO + procurement). Availability: Tue/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks,
Mike Chung
Head of Platform
BrightAI

Hi Mike —

Great to connect — thanks for the clear numbers. Recap & proposed next steps below.

Recap (from call)
- Baseline / peaks as you listed; multi-language model with seasonal spikes.
- Preference for AWS private offer (ok to include GCP/Azure mapping).
- Primary objective: get to a predictable blended $/1M tokens number for budgeting and to evaluate private-offer economics vs Redwood hosted.

How we typically map private offers -> unit economics
1) Marketplace private offer (AWS/GCP/Azure) = list price on our side mapped to a marketplace SKU. Vendor private-offer discounts are passed through; you pay the cloud marketplace invoice.
2) Dedicated/Reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) = SKU + committed throughput; we model the per-1M-token cost taking effective utilization into account (batching, caching).
3) Hosted (Redwood API) = simple per-token unit price (no marketplace), useful for elasticity/short-term spikes.

What I’ll send you (attached)
- unit-mapping template (redwood-unit-mapping-template.xlsx) — map month-by-month volumes against three procurement paths (AWS private offer, Dedicated commit, Hosted API).
- a worked example with your baseline showing crossover points (approx).

Immediate asks from you
- Fill the spreadsheet with month-by-month forecast (your attached usage-forecast.xlsx looks good; we can merge).
- Confirm target budget range / target $/1M tokens (ballpark is fine). That helps prioritize whether we push a larger committed discount vs nominal marketplace pass-through.

Proposed pricing workshop
- Tue 2027-05-18 09:30 PT (45 min) — I’ll invite Marissa (Marketplace specialist) and Vanessa (Dedicated sales) to run the mapping live.

If that works, I’ll send the invite and the template now.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: BrightAI — suggested starting points for unit price mapping

Marissa / Vanessa —

Quick internal note ahead of tomorrow’s workshop with BrightAI. Summary and suggested numbers (back-of-envelope) based on their 250M baseline and peak behavior:

- Baseline 250M tokens/mo -> target unit: $1,000 / 1M tokens (customer indicated budget flexibility but CFO will push).
- Peak 1.2B/day is an outlier; recommend modelling spikes as 5% of month tokens for committed sizing (we can show sensitivity).
- Recommended starting offers to present:
  1) AWS Private Offer (12mo commit): pass-through list price - 20% -> effective ~$800 / 1M tokens (assumes 60% utilization of reserved capacity; margin checks required).
  2) Dedicated Reserved (Redwood Dedicated, 12mo): blended $/1M = ~$650 (higher discount, but needs minimum throughput commit).
  3) Hosted API (on-demand): $1,300 / 1M tokens (for spikes / overflow).

Risks / notes:
- Marketplace private offers sometimes introduce billing lag and need procurement signoff; show them examples of invoice flow.
- We must be explicit about what counts as a token (tokenization differences across models) — include a note in the template.
- If they want cross-cloud parity, we’ll translate the AWS private offer into GCP/Azure equivalents; there’s a small delta for marketplace fees and exchange rates.

I’ll prep a short slide with the sensitivity table and bring the mapping workbook. Vanessa — can you validate the Dedicated blended calc and margin at the numbers above?

Thanks,
Karthik
